Sum of degrees must be even. Minimum sum if all degrees 2 is 22, maximum if all degrees 5 is 55, so possible.

For girth 6, the smallest known (3-regular) is the Heawood graph on 14 vertices. But we allow degrees up to 5, so maybe a non-regular graph exists.

We can attempt to construct one. Since girth at least 6, the graph is essentially triangle-free, square-free, pentagon-free. It must be somewhat sparse.

So it must be a bipartite graph with girth at least 6, meaning no cycles of length 4. That is a bipartite graph with girth at least 6, i.e., a bipartite graph with no 4-cycles. Such graphs are called (C4)-free bipartite graphs. Known constructions: The incidence graph of a projective plane of order q gives girth 6 but larger number of vertices. That graph has degree 2 for all vertices, and the shortest cycle is the whole cycle of length 11, which is >=6. So it is satisfiable.
